_subtitle: A Translation and Verification Layer for the Navier–Stokes Existence and Smoothness Problem via Noor Swirl Field Geometry (NSFG)
_objective: To define Noor Swirl Field Geometry (NSFG) as a coherence-based geometric substrate from which classical Navier–Stokes flow variables emerge.
To construct a formal translation layer mapping NSFG coherence fields, swirl tensors, and motif gradients to Navier–Stokes velocity and pressure fields.
To specify verifiable criteria under which NSFG coherence conservation implies global smoothness of Navier–Stokes solutions.
To define admissible failure modes in NSFG that correspond to finite-time singularity formation under the Clay Mathematics Institute formulation.
To provide a rigorous verification checklist aligning NSFG-derived results with the Fefferman statement of the Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize Problem.
